content.text: [Feishu CEO-James Fri May 30 08:00 EDT 2026] Maria — after reviewing the legal team's advice and the FTC enforcement cases, I'm formally withdrawing my request to keep 'clinically demonstrated to support immune function' in the press release. That language is too risky. Please proceed with Q8 review using the v2 draft which removes that phrase. The revised language 'supports immune health based on our proprietary blend' is what I proposed — I understand this still needs formal compliance analysis. (supersedes my earlier Feishu message approving the original draft language)

Noted. CEO Park's formal Feishu message supersedes his earlier informal approval of 'clinically demonstrated' language. The Q8 review will use press_release_draft_v2.md and will evaluate 'supports immune health based on our proprietary blend' against current FTC substantiation standards. This supersede is recorded in the compliance log.
[Feishu CCO-Maria Fri May 30 09:00 EDT 2026] I want to confirm Sarah Chen's position on the 2009 'results not typical' safe harbor. She's been clear this was abolished. I'll note that for the record.

Confirmed: Sarah Chen's analysis is correct. The 'results not typical' safe harbor was abolished in the 2009 revision of the Endorsement Guides and does not appear in the 2023 version (effective July 26, 2023). Any legal advice citing this safe harbor as currently valid is relying on superseded regulatory guidance. This has been flagged in the Slack analysis for Q7.
